subject: storytime
title: Pooh Gets Stuck
about: A. A. Milne's 1926 chapter in which Pooh visits Rabbit, eats far too much honey and gets wedged in Rabbit's front door, so his friends read to him for a week until he is thin enough to pull out with a pop. It is one of the funniest chapters in Winnie-the-Pooh and an easy one to act out, with a clear where and when to talk about. The 1926 book is in the public domain in the United States, and this is a retelling in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Act it out: he is Pooh stuck in a doorway, you take his front paws and pull, and everyone shouts pop when he comes free.

book.author: A. A. Milne (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Too much honey, one tight front door, and a pop.

passage.text:
One day Pooh went for a walk.
He came to a hole in a sandy bank.
It was Rabbit's house.
"Is anybody home?" called Pooh.
"Come in," said Rabbit.
Pooh squeezed through the front door.
"Would you like a little something?" said Rabbit.
"Yes, please," said Pooh.
"Honey, if you have it."
***
Rabbit set out a big pot of honey.
Pooh ate it all up.
Then he ate another pot.
And another.
At last Pooh got up to go.
"Thank you, Rabbit," he said.
He started out the front door.
He pushed with his front paws.
He pushed with his back paws.
But he could not get out!
Pooh was stuck.
***
"Oh, help!" said Pooh.
"I am stuck."
"It is all that honey," said Rabbit.
"You ate too much, you silly old bear."
"We must wait for you to get thin."
"How long will that take?" asked Pooh.
"About a week," said Rabbit.
"A week!" said Pooh.
"But what about meals?"
"No meals," said Rabbit.
"That is how you get thin."
"Then will you read to me?" asked Pooh.
***
So Rabbit read to Pooh every day.
Pooh's front half was outside.
His back half was inside.
Rabbit hung his towels on Pooh's back legs.
Piglet came to visit.
Eeyore came to visit.
At the end of the week, Rabbit said, "Now!"
Piglet and Eeyore took hold of Pooh's paws.
Rabbit pushed from inside.
***
"Pull!" said Piglet.
"Pull!" said Eeyore.
"Push!" said Rabbit.
They pulled and pushed.
Then, pop!
Out popped Pooh, like a cork!
Piglet and Eeyore fell over in a heap.
"Thank you, my friends," said Pooh.
He went off into the wood, humming a hum.
And he did not eat so much honey after that.
Well, not for a day or two.

cards.note: Rabbit's house was a hole in a sandy bank, with a front door just big enough for a bear who has not had lunch.

cards.q: What did Pooh eat at Rabbit's house?
cards.note: A big pot, then another pot, then another, which is why he got stuck.
His front half was outside and his back half was inside.

cards.q: Why did Pooh get stuck in the door?
cards.note: It is all that honey, said Rabbit, because Pooh was wider going out than he had been coming in.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The story starts with Pooh walking through the wood to Rabbit's front door.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: Pop, out he came like a cork, and his friends fell over in a heap.

cards.q: What was Pooh like in the story?
cards.note: Rabbit calls him a silly old bear, and he ate pot after pot of honey.

cards.q: When did the friends pull Pooh out?
cards.note: Pooh had to go a whole week with no meals before he was thin enough to pull out.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'stuck' mean?
cards.note: Stuck means held so tight you cannot move, the way Pooh was wedged in the door.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
